summary:
FirePulse is an interactive wildfire monitoring and analysis dashboard that transforms NASA FIRMS satellite fire detections into meaningful visual insights. We developed a web-based platform that allows users to explore active-fire observations across different geographical regions, select satellite sensors, and analyze activity over custom date ranges.

FirePulse combines an interactive hotspot map with a heatmap visualization, a daily Burning Activity Calendar, an activity timeline with moving averages, and comparisons between MODIS and VIIRS satellite observations. It also uses statistical anomaly detection to identify days when fire detections are unusually high compared to normal activity.

By turning raw satellite data into accessible visualizations, FirePulse makes it easier to explore where fire activity is occurring, understand how it changes over time, and identify unusual patterns that may deserve further investigation.

Our goal is to make NASA's publicly available Earth-observation data more understandable and useful for wildfire monitoring and analysis.
details:
Project Details — FirePulse

What does FirePulse do and how does it work?

FirePulse is an interactive wildfire monitoring and analysis dashboard that transforms NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System) satellite observations into understandable visual insights.

Users can select predefined geographical regions, including South Asia, Europe, Australia, the Amazon Basin and Continental US, or draw a custom area directly on the map. They can select supported satellite sensors and a date range to retrieve active-fire observations.

The platform processes the returned data and presents it through several interactive features:

  • Interactive Fire Map: Displays individual satellite fire detections and provides a heatmap mode to visualize the spatial concentration of fire activity.
  • Burning Activity Calendar: Shows daily hotspot counts in a calendar-style heatmap, making changes in activity easier to identify.
  • Activity Timeline: Visualizes daily fire detections and moving-average trends over the selected period.
  • Satellite Sensor Comparison: Allows users to compare observations from MODIS and VIIRS instruments aboard different satellites.
  • Anomaly Detection: Uses statistical analysis of daily hotspot counts to flag unusually high activity. Days with a z-score greater than 2 are identified as potential anomalies.

What are its benefits and intended impact?

Raw satellite datasets can be difficult to interpret, especially for people who are unfamiliar with scientific data formats. FirePulse addresses this challenge by bringing geographical exploration, historical activity patterns and statistical analysis together in one accessible interface.

Its intended impact is to help users explore fire activity, understand changes over time and identify unusual patterns that may deserve further investigation. It can support educational activities, environmental research and preliminary wildfire monitoring.

FirePulse is an analytical and visualization tool. Its hotspot detections and statistical alerts are not confirmations of ground fires or predictions of future wildfire events.

Tools and technologies used

We developed FirePulse using the following technologies:

Frontend:

  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript
  • Leaflet.js for interactive mapping
  • Leaflet.draw for custom geographical selection
  • Leaflet.heat for heatmap visualization
  • Chart.js for activity timelines and data comparisons
  • Esri World Imagery for satellite basemap imagery

Backend:

  • Python
  • Python standard library for the backend server
  • NASA FIRMS Area API for active-fire satellite observations
  • HTTP-based communication between the frontend and backend

Data sources:

  • MODIS Near Real-Time observations from Terra and Aqua
  • VIIRS NOAA-20 Near Real-Time observations
  • VIIRS NOAA-21 Near Real-Time observations

Development and deployment:

  • Git and GitHub for version control and source-code management
  • Render for cloud hosting and deployment

What makes FirePulse creative?

FirePulse combines multiple ways of understanding satellite fire observations instead of presenting users with only a map or a collection of raw records.

Its combination of spatial heatmaps, a GitHub-style Burning Activity Calendar, moving-average timelines, satellite sensor comparisons and statistical anomaly detection provides different perspectives on the same underlying dataset.

The ability to explore custom geographical areas and compare different satellite sources makes the platform flexible for different regions and investigation periods.

Factors considered during development

Our team considered several important factors:

  1. Data reliability: Using NASA FIRMS as the primary source of active-fire observations.
  2. Accessibility: Designing visualizations that make complex satellite data easier to understand.
  3. Performance: Handling large datasets through bounded requests, concurrency controls and response-size limits.
  4. Security: Sending the NASA FIRMS API key through a request header rather than exposing it in URLs.
  5. Usability: Providing region presets, custom area selection, sensor filters and interactive map controls.
  6. Scientific interpretation: Treating anomaly detection as a statistical indicator rather than a fire prediction or confirmed event.

Our Vision

With FirePulse, we aim to make satellite-based fire information more accessible and understandable. By transforming NASA Earth-observation data into interactive visual insights, we hope to support better exploration, awareness and investigation of wildfire activity.
